added_failures_note: unmeasured: the reviewed manifest names no base gate log, so the added-failure count was not taken

tests/test_a_reload_runs_the_committed_h.would_fail_if: the reloader starts with a stamp other than the fixture repository first commit
a new source commit does not produce exactly one re-exec
the re-exec imports directly from the editable source root
the extracted image contains the uncommitted value or lacks the second committed value
the exec root omits the second commit or loses the original source root or image commit in its environment
the restarted reloader does not retain the extracted root, original source root, and second image commit respectively
a third source commit does not trigger a second exec onto a distinct root holding that commit and its expected bytes; the source-root mutation log confirms line 128 becomes red
a committed module that fails to import does not name the refusal and missing dependency, or is nevertheless executed
an archive timeout is not reported as a materialization failure with a timeout reason or is nevertheless executed
each new commit fails to produce one exec or its extracted content is not that iteration expected literal
retention does not delete only the oldest tree or does not print that deletion; these checks do not protect a tree still in use

tests/test_a_reload_waits_for_a_clean_tr.would_fail_if: a tracked uncommitted edit changes the source commit stamp or triggers a reload
the live producer emits either dirty-tree or other reload deferral while handling the uncommitted edit
the commit leaves the stamp fixed, the re-exec command lacks its new commit, or it materializes zero or multiple roots for that commit
the cache bytes differ from the same working file the fixture supplied; copying that working file rather than HEAD would remain green, so this assertion is not an independent provenance guard

tests/test_stale_producer_warning_waits_.would_fail_if: the follower, snapshot, or seat reader gives a stamp different from the Git first commit
a seat deliberately planted at the current commit is reported stale or emits the warning
the follower, snapshot, or seat reader fails to observe the Git second commit
the planted seat stamp changes when the source commit changes
a seat planted at the first commit is not classified stale or fails to emit a warning after the second commit

findings.text: blocking: Pruning removes every cache tree past the newest three without checking whether a live follower or producer still executes from it; a deferred or slow process can lose its import root, and later imports can fail while the process is meant to keep running.

follow-on: The producer seat records follower_code_stamp(), which now reads source HEAD rather than the carried image commit; a new commit between extraction and seat registration can label an older running image current and suppress the stale-producer warning until a later poll.

follow-on: The assertion compares cached ticker bytes with the working ticker file the fixture handed to the reload after committing it, so copying that working file would keep the assertion green; compare against git show HEAD or dirty the file again before checking cached bytes.
